text:
Mark Jankowski has 10 goals in 17 games. He's 32, he's on his fifth NHL team, and before this season he had 79 goals in 482 career games. Carolina's depth center, a Stanley Cup winner with the Hurricanes last spring, is scoring like a top-six winger, and almost all of it is goals: he has one assist.

Some of this is earned. His own chances are up to 1.37 expected goals per 60 (a measure of chance quality) from 0.90 last season, his ice time is up nearly two minutes a night over his last ten, and that stretch includes two goals in Saturday's win over Seattle. But he's shooting 28% after 17% last season, and that's the part that rarely lasts: 10 goals on 5.69 expected. Evolving-Hockey's numbers from last season describe him as a defensive forward first, one who took chances away at the 92nd percentile, and the tools (skating speed and shot velocity both in the bottom fifth of the league) say the same. Enjoy the run for what it is: a reliable checker getting rewarded, with the finishing likely to come back toward his usual level.
